name: Hosts and the fungi on them

citation.text: Põlme, S., Abarenkov, K., Nilsson, R. H., et al. (2020). FungalTraits: a user-friendly traits database of fungi and fungus-like stramenopiles. Fungal Diversity, 105, 1–16.

description: The other side of the same table: hosts, from whole kingdoms to single genera, drawn as dots, and grouped by the fungal genera that live on more than one of them, such as the moulds that eat both nematodes and rotifers, or both mosses and liverworts.

image.credit: Mitch from Costa Mesa, CA, USA

links.partner: A2723.1. Discontented pine-tree: cause of pine needles. Pine tree given silk leaves, glass leaves, etc. Always discontented. Finally has needles again. (Cf. A2767.1.)
F232.1.2. Fairy has back rough like pine cone.
F451.4.3.5. Floors in dwarf home are covered with pine twigs.
G314. Pine bender. Kills victims by springing tree.
J242.2. Pine and thornbush dispute as to their usefulness. Beauty of form does not give worth; pine grows slowly but it will withstand storms.
X1203. Lie: animal's food affects him in unusual way. (E.g. Pine tops: milk good for cough syrup.)
Z39.4.2. Sparrow, where are you going? – To eat seed. – The owner will scold you. – I'll sit on a pine tree. – etc.
